messages.author: edee7056cab8dca0
messages.subject: Heterozygotes and QTLs
parts:
Hi Karl,

I have a RIL population that has fairly messy data. For some reason, there is a large percentage of heterozygous genotypes for the generation of the individuals (~20%). After much manual curation of the data, i've been able to construct a genetic map using the physical positions as a reference for marker order. This has left me with a handful of markers in good agreement using maximum likelihood, regression mapping and physical positions.

My first question is, i if want to read the data as a backcross (which obviously gives me a warning for having too many genotype classes) and use convert2riself and omit all of those heterozygotes, then use mqmaugment or sim.geno to impute them, what would be the implications in terms of my QTL detections for MQM (or any any analysis)?

My second question is, what are the implications of eliminating identical/problematic individuals for map construction and then restoring the excluded ones for qtl analysis in the effort to have more phenotypic data (my population size is small)?

Thank you,

Valerio

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Heterozygotes and QTLs
parts:
Regarding the heterozygous genotypes: It's hard to say what the implications are. It depends upon whether these heterozygous genotypes are errors or are real.

Regarding the problematic individuals: I would try the QTL analysis both with and without them.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Heterozygotes and QTLs
parts:
R/qtl can't handle heterozygous genotypes in RIL. It simply omits them.
That you are getting similar results in winqtlcart and R/qtl is comforting.

karl
